title: Kernel handoff stability bridge: graded prefill + telemetry gates for v2/v3 mix
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Investigate and implement a lightweight "bridge" layer that smooths kernel handoffs between FlashAttention v2 and v3 at startup and during prefill->decode transitions. The goal is to eliminate a class of intermittent latency spikes and correctness regressions observed when the runtime switches kernels aggressively for mixed workloads (long context prefill followed by short decode bursts). The bridge will provide graded prefill pacing, handshake token alignment for KV cache layouts, and telemetry gates to avoid activating v3 paths until warmed and validated per-host and per-tenant.
acceptance_criteria: No unexplained p95 decode latency regressions in production canaries after enabling bridge in canary pool (compare to baseline)
End-to-end token correctness (sampling logits and ngram outputs) matches baseline for 10k generated sequences per model variant
Canary rollout plan with per-host gating and auto-rollback triggers defined and automated
Bridge adds <4% CPU overhead at steady-state and does not increase average per-token GPU time by >2%
Automated unit and integration tests covering handshake token evolution, workspace reservation backstop, and graded pacing logic
investigation_notes: Prod incidents: Two customer incidents on 2025-08-21 and 2025-08-29 where p95 decode latency increased 1.6x for models with 8k+ prefill contexts. Root cause: kernel oscillation and KV-cache layout mismatch during aggressive v3 activation.
Reproduced locally with synthetic replay: sequence of prefill 6k tokens then decode 1-3 tokens triggers warmup thrash on v3 when workspace allocator attempts microtiling changes mid-decode.
Hypothesis: v3's improved tiling layout requires transient workspace reallocation which, when coupled with immediate decode, causes eviction/rebuild churn and kernel-choice flip-flops.
Previous mitigations (prefill pacing, warmup shims) reduced but did not eliminate cases; need per-host warmup curves + a negotiation layer.
Telemetry shows median time-to-first-stable-v3 of ~350ms on some GPU generations and >1s on others under bursty arrival patterns. These hosts should be gated longer.
experiments: Experiment A (local): Introduced 50ms graded prefill pause between prefill end and decode start -> reduced p95 by ~18% in synthetic replay but visible throughput cost for low-latency use cases.

Experiment B (canary on internal cluster): Handshake token that encodes workspace layout version and KV cache epoch. Decoder waits for token match or a short graded timeout -> eliminated ~75% of latency spikes in canary (100 hosts), p50 unchanged.
Experiment C (telemetry gate): Require v3 activation only after telemetry signal 'stable_kernels=3' observed for 30s per host -> safe but raised steady-state latency by 1.5% on worst-case hardware.
Combined approach (bridge): handshake token + graded prefill pacing + telemetry gate with adaptive timeouts tuned by host profile yields best tradeoff: spike elimination with <2% steady-state cost.
decisions: Implement bridge as a thin runtime shim (no model change) that negotiates kernel activation using a handshake token and per-host warmup counters.
Use telemetry-derived host profiles to pick graded timeouts instead of a single conservative global timeout.
Expose an operator flag to force-enable v3 for debugging and an automatic rollback when specified regression metrics cross thresholds for 5 minutes.
Keep bridge enabled in default canary pool for one week of sustained observations before broader rollout.
